Summarize the following document in 150 to 200 words for a reader who has not seen it. Be accurate and neutral. Return only the summary.

---
GAZA, (PIC)
On the 43rd anniversary of the Sabra and Shatila massacre, the Israeli occupation army chose to announce the beginning of its large-scale assault on Gaza City. This announcement contained nothing new except for its usual misleading language. The Israeli aggression has continued relentlessly for 23 months, but perhaps what is new is that Israel now declares its project more explicitly, more defiantly, and more brazenly: genocide, destruction, and displacement of the Palestinian people.
Since the Nakba, acts of extermination and uprooting have been repeatedly carried out, from Deir Yassin in 1948 to Kafr Qasim in 1956, from Sabra and Shatila in 1982 to the ongoing annihilation of Gaza, turning the Nakba into an ongoing reality and making today’s events a continuation of a bloody colonial path from which Israel has long escaped punishment and accountability.
Since October 2023, Israel has been waging a full-scale war of extermination against the Palestinian people in Gaza, leaving over 250,000 people dead or wounded, numbers now acknowledged by Israeli leaders themselves with sadism and arrogance, after they had long dismissed them when they came from Gaza’s Ministry of Health. Entire cities and neighborhoods have been leveled, millions of tons of rubble have buried landmarks and homes, the environment has been poisoned, and the Strip has been turned into a hazardous wasteland for years to come.
A global human heritage
Gaza, with its small area of just 365 km², is not merely a besieged piece of land but a global human heritage extending back thousands of years. It is one of the world’s oldest inhabited cities, with roots dating back more than three millennia. It was home to the Canaanites and the ancient Philistines and served as a strategic hub on global trade routes linking Egypt and the Levant, a gateway between Asia and Africa.
Gaza holds unique historical monuments, mosques, churches, and old markets that form a continuous human memory. Their destruction is a major cultural crime that goes beyond Palestinians and strikes at all of humanity, erasing a long record of creativity and cultural diversity.
But the danger of genocide is not limited to historical heritage. Gaza has long been known for its unyielding resilience, standing tall against invaders throughout history. This deeply rooted steadfastness has made it a forward fortress protecting its Arab and Islamic surroundings and a symbol of rising from the rubble. The gravest danger today is that Israel seeks to break this resilience by destroying its people and all means of life so that the city remains without memory, without the ability to rise again.
The Israeli eradication mindset haunts the Palestinian across all his historic land. The occupier declares itself a “Jewish state” that recognizes neither the Palestinian nor his existence or his land, and today imposes what it calls the enforcement of “sovereignty” over the West Bank, completely tied to the attempt to empty Gaza of its population. The cause is one, and the goal is one: the expulsion of the Palestinian people.
A global threat
The aggression on Gaza is not isolated from its regional context. In parallel, Israel has launched blatant attacks on several Arab and Muslim countries and has threatened others, as part of its “Greater Israel” project reproducing a colonial discourse that threatens the entire region. The facts reveal that the issue is not just “Hamas,” but a project of domination that destabilizes the entire Levant and extends to the Red Sea and the Gulf.
Israel has today transformed from a mere occupying power into a global threat beyond the borders of Palestine. Its continued genocide, siege, and starvation of Gaza despite International Court of Justice orders exposes the collapse of the international legal system and undermines the principle of prohibiting land acquisition by force, a cornerstone of the post–World War II order. The open American and Western military support not only shields Israel but risks turning the world into a new arena of global chaos.
Deceptive negotiations
Over the past two years, Israel, in collaboration with the United States, has used negotiations as a cover to prolong the war. It discarded and broke the March 2025 agreement when it reneged on its commitments and continued its aggression. Since then, the same pattern has repeated: successive proposals that it either rejects or stalls on, promises of ceasefires that turn into traps, and even direct targeting of negotiators through airstrikes and assassinations including the negotiators themselves in a flagrant violation of basic diplomatic norms.
The so-called political track has become nothing more than a smokescreen to mislead international opinion and portray Israel as a “negotiating party” rather than a war criminal using negotiations as a tool to buy time, reposition militarily, and continue its aggression without paying any real political price.
Collapse of the Israeli propaganda
Alongside its field crimes, Israel wages a parallel media war aimed at falsifying facts and fabricating an alternative narrative that downplays the scale of the catastrophe it is committing. It has assassinated around 250 Palestinian journalists and barred global media from entering Gaza so that it alone controls the narrative. But it has failed. Thousands of images and testimonies have emerged, revealing the genocide in real time, exposing its deceit before the entire world.
While Israeli discourse continues to push the misleading claim that it is fighting “Hamas” to retrieve what it calls “hostages,” the truth is that these captives are merely occupying soldiers captured by the resistance after participating in killing and bombing Palestinians. Their presence in the Gaza envelope before October 7 was a continuation of four bloody wars Israel had already waged against the Strip. What is happening today is merely the continuation of that path, but in its most horrific form: a systematic war of extermination, forced displacement, and an attempt to erase Palestinian existence altogether.
The cliché of Israeli propaganda has collapsed before the facts, along with Western media complicity: “Israel’s right to self-defense.” What right can be built on falsehood and deny a people’s very existence on their land? This pretext has fallen, revealing itself as nothing more than a rehashed version of the colonial myth: “a land without a people for a people without a land.” It is a deceptive formula that justifies killing and grants a false cover to an ongoing occupation, in blatant violation of international law. According to human rights principles and charters, an occupier has no “right to self-defense” against the people under its occupation.
Gaza as a global symbol of liberation
Gaza is no longer merely a Palestinian city but a global symbol of liberation and resilience, a warning bell reminding the world that complicity in genocide will not go unchallenged. Its steadfastness protects Palestinians from annihilation, but also blocks broader expansionist projects that threaten the entire region and the world.
And Gaza is no longer alone. Waves of global solidarity have swept across five continents, from New York to London, Cape Town, and Sydney, confirming that the Palestinian cause has become a unifying human conscience. Millions have taken to the streets in the largest protests since the Vietnam War, demanding an end to the genocide and rejecting international silence.
Beyond the streets, striking stances by artists, thinkers, and global influencers have shifted public opinion, opened new horizons for freedom, and broken the traditional media monopoly that long shielded Israel. This popular and cultural solidarity goes beyond empathy it is shaping a new global consciousness that sees Gaza as a symbol of the fight against colonialism and genocide, and against a global system built on double standards.

GAZA, (PIC)
On the 43rd anniversary of the Sabra and Shatila massacre, the Israeli occupation army chose to announce the beginning of its large-scale assault on Gaza City. This announcement contained nothing new except for its usual misleading language. The Israeli aggression has continued relentlessly for 23 months, but perhaps what is new is that Israel now declares its project more explicitly, more defiantly, and more brazenly: genocide, destruction, and displacement of the Palestinian people.
Since the Nakba, acts of extermination and uprooting have been repeatedly carried out, from Deir Yassin in 1948 to Kafr Qasim in 1956, from Sabra and Shatila in 1982 to the ongoing annihilation of Gaza, turning the Nakba into an ongoing reality and making today’s events a continuation of a bloody colonial path from which Israel has long escaped punishment and accountability.
Since October 2023, Israel has been waging a full-scale war of extermination against the Palestinian people in Gaza, leaving over 250,000 people dead or wounded, numbers now acknowledged by Israeli leaders themselves with sadism and arrogance, after they had long dismissed them when they came from Gaza’s Ministry of Health. Entire cities and neighborhoods have been leveled, millions of tons of rubble have buried landmarks and homes, the environment has been poisoned, and the Strip has been turned into a hazardous wasteland for years to come.
A global human heritage
Gaza, with its small area of just 365 km², is not merely a besieged piece of land but a global human heritage extending back thousands of years. It is one of the world’s oldest inhabited cities, with roots dating back more than three millennia. It was home to the Canaanites and the ancient Philistines and served as a strategic hub on global trade routes linking Egypt and the Levant, a gateway between Asia and Africa.
Gaza holds unique historical monuments, mosques, churches, and old markets that form a continuous human memory. Their destruction is a major cultural crime that goes beyond Palestinians and strikes at all of humanity, erasing a long record of creativity and cultural diversity.
But the danger of genocide is not limited to historical heritage. Gaza has long been known for its unyielding resilience, standing tall against invaders throughout history. This deeply rooted steadfastness has made it a forward fortress protecting its Arab and Islamic surroundings and a symbol of rising from the rubble. The gravest danger today is that Israel seeks to break this resilience by destroying its people and all means of life so that the city remains without memory, without the ability to rise again.
The Israeli eradication mindset haunts the Palestinian across all his historic land. The occupier declares itself a “Jewish state” that recognizes neither the Palestinian nor his existence or his land, and today imposes what it calls the enforcement of “sovereignty” over the West Bank, completely tied to the attempt to empty Gaza of its population. The cause is one, and the goal is one: the expulsion of the Palestinian people.
A global threat
The aggression on Gaza is not isolated from its regional context. In parallel, Israel has launched blatant attacks on several Arab and Muslim countries and has threatened others, as part of its “Greater Israel” project reproducing a colonial discourse that threatens the entire region. The facts reveal that the issue is not just “Hamas,” but a project of domination that destabilizes the entire Levant and extends to the Red Sea and the Gulf.
Israel has today transformed from a mere occupying power into a global threat beyond the borders of Palestine. Its continued genocide, siege, and starvation of Gaza despite International Court of Justice orders exposes the collapse of the international legal system and undermines the principle of prohibiting land acquisition by force, a cornerstone of the post–World War II order. The open American and Western military support not only shields Israel but risks turning the world into a new arena of global chaos.
Deceptive negotiations
Over the past two years, Israel, in collaboration with the United States, has used negotiations as a cover to prolong the war. It discarded and broke the March 2025 agreement when it reneged on its commitments and continued its aggression. Since then, the same pattern has repeated: successive proposals that it either rejects or stalls on, promises of ceasefires that turn into traps, and even direct targeting of negotiators through airstrikes and assassinations including the negotiators themselves in a flagrant violation of basic diplomatic norms.
The so-called political track has become nothing more than a smokescreen to mislead international opinion and portray Israel as a “negotiating party” rather than a war criminal using negotiations as a tool to buy time, reposition militarily, and continue its aggression without paying any real political price.
Collapse of the Israeli propaganda
Alongside its field crimes, Israel wages a parallel media war aimed at falsifying facts and fabricating an alternative narrative that downplays the scale of the catastrophe it is committing. It has assassinated around 250 Palestinian journalists and barred global media from entering Gaza so that it alone controls the narrative. But it has failed. Thousands of images and testimonies have emerged, revealing the genocide in real time, exposing its deceit before the entire world.
While Israeli discourse continues to push the misleading claim that it is fighting “Hamas” to retrieve what it calls “hostages,” the truth is that these captives are merely occupying soldiers captured by the resistance after participating in killing and bombing Palestinians. Their presence in the Gaza envelope before October 7 was a continuation of four bloody wars Israel had already waged against the Strip. What is happening today is merely the continuation of that path, but in its most horrific form: a systematic war of extermination, forced displacement, and an attempt to erase Palestinian existence altogether.
The cliché of Israeli propaganda has collapsed before the facts, along with Western media complicity: “Israel’s right to self-defense.” What right can be built on falsehood and deny a people’s very existence on their land? This pretext has fallen, revealing itself as nothing more than a rehashed version of the colonial myth: “a land without a people for a people without a land.” It is a deceptive formula that justifies killing and grants a false cover to an ongoing occupation, in blatant violation of international law. According to human rights principles and charters, an occupier has no “right to self-defense” against the people under its occupation.
Gaza as a global symbol of liberation
Gaza is no longer merely a Palestinian city but a global symbol of liberation and resilience, a warning bell reminding the world that complicity in genocide will not go unchallenged. Its steadfastness protects Palestinians from annihilation, but also blocks broader expansionist projects that threaten the entire region and the world.
And Gaza is no longer alone. Waves of global solidarity have swept across five continents, from New York to London, Cape Town, and Sydney, confirming that the Palestinian cause has become a unifying human conscience. Millions have taken to the streets in the largest protests since the Vietnam War, demanding an end to the genocide and rejecting international silence.
Beyond the streets, striking stances by artists, thinkers, and global influencers have shifted public opinion, opened new horizons for freedom, and broken the traditional media monopoly that long shielded Israel. This popular and cultural solidarity goes beyond empathy it is shaping a new global consciousness that sees Gaza as a symbol of the fight against colonialism and genocide, and against a global system built on double standards.
